inputs: issue #2129 body and maintainer reply (github.com page, fetched 2026-11-14)
prompt:
You are a code-review claim extractor. You do NOT judge whether the change is good.
Produce the minimal set of falsifiable claims this change makes or must satisfy.
Rules:
1. Every requirement item (F*, NF*, S*) must be covered by >=1 claim, or listed in uncovered_requirements.
2. Statements from the commit message, README or docs written by the author agent are
   CLAIMS TO TEST (source="author-narrative"), never evidence.
3. Every claim must cite >=1 exact diff line: {path, new_line, quote}. Quote must be verbatim.
4. For each claim propose a verifier: timemachine | xray | regen | matrix | static | argued.
5. Never output confidence numbers or words like "likely correct".
Output JSON matching the schema. No prose.

claims.text: A partial class marked [GeneratedMessagePackFormatter] that implements IMessagePackFormatter<T> for a type T from another assembly gets its Serialize and Deserialize members generated in the consuming project.
claims.verifier_notes: Execution tests build only when the generator writes the bodies (they fail to build on base).

claims.text: Without a surrogate, the generated formatter writes every public read-write instance property and field of T as a string-keyed map entry named after the member.
claims.verifier_notes: Probe runs/2129/probe/*.txt compares the wire output with ContractlessStandardResolver.

claims.text: Attributes that are present on T are used for the wire contract.

citations.quote: By default the formatter serializes the type in *contractless* mode

claims.verifier_notes: The collector never reads attributes on T; only a surrogate type carries [Key] and [IgnoreMember]. The maintainer's reply asked for the attribute-first behaviour.

claims.text: The generated resolver registers each generated formatter, so GeneratedMessagePackResolver.Instance returns it for the formatted type.
The fixture assembly that declares the formatted types has no MessagePack reference, so the feature works without adding anything to the assembly that owns T.

citations.quote: This assembly deliberately does NOT reference MessagePack.

claims.text: Hand-written formatters and existing generated formatters are unaffected: the exclusion in the formatter search only matches classes carrying the new attribute, and the template keeps 'internal sealed class' for every other formatter.
The new attribute, the four analyzer diagnostics and the surrogate option are documented in the README, in per-diagnostic pages and in the analyzer release notes.

citations.quote: ### Formatters for types from other assemblies
MsgPack019 | Usage | Error | Generated formatter must be partial

claims.text: Only public read-write members are written. Read-only members and members with a non-public setter are skipped, and no diagnostic says so.

citations.quote: Read-only members are skipped because they cannot be deserialized.

claims.text: Misuse of the attribute is reported as a compile error: a non-partial formatter (MsgPack019), a class that does not implement IMessagePackFormatter<T> (MsgPack020), an abstract type (MsgPack021) and surrogate mismatches (MsgPack022, MsgPack005).
A surrogate type's [Key] and [IgnoreMember] attributes decide which members are written and under which keys, with members matched by name and type.
Adding the public attribute class GeneratedMessagePackFormatterAttribute to the MessagePack.Annotations assembly is additive and does not change existing public API.

coverage_gaps: The issue's second and third alternatives (user-defined attribute copies, generated attributes) are not implemented and not claimed.
No claim covers generic types, abstract types, unions or constructor-only types: the README lists them as unsupported and MsgPack021 / NoDeserializingConstructor reject them.
Only classes and structs with public members were exercised end to end; nested types, base-class members and indexers have no test.
